clarity_basis: All 26 papers in this compilation that print a Gorilla name print 'Gorilla gorilla'; none prints a subspecies and none prints beringei. The string is therefore clear at species rank and silent below it.
inference_basis: G. g. gorilla is the nominate subspecies of G. gorilla and the only one present in research collections; G. g. diehli numbers a few hundred wild individuals and is not represented in brain collections.
note: Resolves inconsistently downstream. Six merges (GLI, behaviour, cell_morphology, cellcounts, gyrification, weights) keep 'Gorilla gorilla'; __merging_volumes lumps all 110 rows to 'Gorilla sp.'; and __merging_endocranial_volume splits the SAME printed name INTERNALLY - one row to 'Gorilla gorilla' (ECV 490.41, species_basis=hub) and one to 'Gorilla sp.' (ECV 461.0, species_basis=lump). The internal split is the actual defect. See taxon_clarity_observed.csv resolves_to, where that pair is one of 11 printed names resolving more than one way.

clarity_basis: Prints 'Gorilla gorilla'; the cell-count merge keeps it as such rather than lumping to 'Gorilla sp.'.
inference_basis: Same as the default row; recorded separately because this paper is the one Gorilla source NOT lumped to 'Gorilla sp.'.
note: Kept as its own row to document that this paper's values are among those the cell-count merge does NOT lump; the judgement is identical to the wildcard row.

clarity_basis: Four papers print the bare binomial: Haarlem_etal_2026 (critical flicker fusion), Heffner_Heffner_1992_a (hearing), Koay_etal_1998 (hearing), Veilleux_Kirk_2014 (vision). All are laboratory psychophysics; none states wild or domestic.
inference_basis: Laboratory psychophysics on pigs uses domestic animals; no wild-boar colony is implied by any of the four. Not raised to high because none of the four states the form.
note: If confirmed per paper, these 4 sources should be relabelled at source rather than pooled downstream; that would let the cohort count them without averaging wild and domestic masses.

clarity_basis: Prints the domestic form explicitly; 16 papers, incl. Kazu_etal_2015 and HerculanoHouzel_etal_2015 Tables 1-5.
inference_basis: Printed name is already the form-level name; no inference needed.

clarity_basis: Five papers print the bare binomial (Ashwell_2020, Bush_Allman_2003, Heffner_Heffner_1992_a, Koay_etal_1998, Veilleux_Kirk_2014); a disjoint five print 'furo'.
inference_basis: Bush_Allman_2003_Table1 prints 'Mustela putorius' and Bush_Allman_2004_a_Table2 prints 'Mustela putorius furo', both reporting Neocortex_grey_matter_Vol.mm3 = 2140. One lab published one specimen under both names in consecutive papers, so the bare binomial here denotes the domestic ferret.
note: This is positive evidence the two ferret labels are one animal, which argues for pooling; the cohort currently leaves them separate pending owner sign-off.

clarity_basis: Table1 prints 'Mustela putorius'. The same lab's Bush_Allman_2004_a_Table2 prints 'Mustela putorius furo' for the identical Neocortex_grey_matter_Vol.mm3 = 2140.
inference_basis: Identical value under both names from one lab in consecutive years; same specimen.
note: The decisive row for the ferret; do not pool the ferret without citing it.

clarity_basis: Prints the domestic form explicitly; 5 papers, incl. JardimMesseder_etal_2017.
inference_basis: Printed name is already the form-level name.

clarity_basis: 36 papers print 'Saimiri sciureus'; none prints boliviensis. The name is unambiguous AS PRINTED.
inference_basis: Taken at face value. Whether the historical material is in fact S. boliviensis is a re-identification question about specimens, not a clarity question about the name, and is not settled here.
note: Do NOT read this row as evidence against the boliviensis re-identification; it only records that the printed name is determinate. See _keys/reidentifications.csv.
